text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Helm Labs (tenant helm-42) — increased auth failures observed across their VPC private pool. ~18% auth errors -> service impact on dedicated pool helm-vpc-us-east. Paging SRE oncall. Incident link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/I-2026-1718200000

pagerduty: PagerDuty alerted SRE oncall group: SRE (primary: mike.sre). Escalation started.

alice.nguyen: I'm taking incident lead. @mike.sre are you free to dive in? I'll coordinate with support and legal.

mike.sre: I'm on. Pulling logs from auth-proxy and router. Seeing a bunch of TLS handshake failures: `tls handshake error: remote error: bad certificate` from connections to customer OIDC at 203.0.113.45.

irene.support: Helm Labs reported: "we're seeing 502s to Redwood API auth for our service, started ~12:12 UTC". They gave correlation id `helm-42/2026-03-12/xyz`.

alice.nguyen: Priority: reduce customer 502s. Two immediate mitigations: 1) route Helm traffic to hosted auth-fallback (warm standby), 2) try to accept their presented cert chain temporarily (risky). Need customer permission for fallback since they're on private contract.

tom.platform: we can flip routing flag for that tenant but legal requires opt-in for sending identity data to hosted plane. I'll loop legal/support.

mike.sre: digging deeper — JWKS fetch from their OIDC returns 403 in some upstream calls and our mTLS agent logs `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. Also `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate` in openssl. I suspect missing intermediate CA in their rotation.

irene.support: Confirmed with customer on Slack: they rotated certificates earlier today and "we may have omitted an intermediate certificate in the chain". They can push corrected chain but need ~20-30m.

alice.nguyen: OK. Ask customer to push corrected chain. Meanwhile we need immediate mitigation. Tom — can legal approve emergency fallback so we can route auth to hosted for 30m?

tom.platform: Legal verbal signoff is allowed for emergency fallback. Support to record explicit customer consent in ticket.

irene.support: Customer verbally approves fallback for 30 minutes to restore traffic. Recording consent in ticket #SUP-112233.

mike.sre: Executing routing change now: `redwood-cli route set --tenant helm-42 --auth-mode hosted-fallback --region us-east-1 --confirm` (running).

devops-bot: deploy-bot: route config update started id=rte-97abc, targeting router-2, router-3, rollout window 60s.

alice.nguyen: Mike, monitor auth success rates and client handshake logs. I'll keep customer updated.

mike.sre: tailing auth logs — seeing immediate drop in TLS handshake errors for helm-42. Auth success > 99% now. :white_check_mark: Error rate down to <1%.

irene.support: Helm Labs confirms in their channel: "errors cleared, our traffic is back to normal". They will push the fixed cert chain and confirm when done.

ben.runtime: Notes for post-incident: 1) Add runtime validation during customer cert registration to detect missing intermediate CA. 2) Enhance diagnostic message to customers: "chain incomplete / missing intermediate" instead of generic TLS error. 3) Add an automatic pre-rotation checker for tenant-managed cert updates.

alice.nguyen: Agreed. Action items: Support to get proof of fix from customer and close fallback within 30m; Engineering to add onboarding/runtime validation and better error telemetry; Product to update contract templates to cover emergency fallback behavior more explicitly.

tom.platform: I'll create a follow-up ticket to examine our routing flags and make sure there is audit + TTL on emergency fallbacks.

mike.sre: Handing over active monitoring to night oncall @sarah-sre in 30m. Sarah, when they re-enable private auth, please validate the full chain with `openssl s_client -connect <oidc-host>:443 -showcerts` and ensure `verify return:1`.

sarah-sre: ack, will take over monitoring and confirm before any flip back.

incident-bot: Incident record created: I-2026-1718200000 — "Helm Labs tenant: VPC auth failures; emergency hosted-auth fallback applied". Severity: Sev2. Owner: alice.nguyen. Postmortem ETA: 72h.

alice.nguyen: Quick timeline for postmortem: root cause = customer rotated cert without intermediate; immediate mitigation = hosted fallback with customer consent; corrective = onboarding checks + runbook updates. I'll open the postmortem doc and DM assignees. Thanks team. :pray:

mike.sre: final note before handoff — we should add a health check alert specifically for `x509: unable to get local issuer certificate` on tenant auth paths so this is surfaced before customers see 502s.

alice.nguyen: Agreed. Adding to action list. Closing incident channel when Sarah confirms route flip status and customer cert verification.
